intro: Adán writes and lectures on liturgy, hymnody, and the sacred music of Latin America. He is a columnist for GIA Publications, edits Puentes for the Hymn Society's Center for Congregational Song, and is managing editor of Res facta. His choral music is published by MusicSpoke and GIA.

featured.title: The Precedent for Vernacular and Multilingual Liturgies in the Catholic Church in Latin America
featured.blurb: How folk Masses in local languages, from the Misa Campesina onward, grew out of Vatican II and became a form of theological and cultural resistance in Latin America. Peer-reviewed, open access.

featured.title: Liberationist Perspectives on the Misa Criolla by Ariel Ramírez
featured.blurb: A reading of the best-known Latin American Mass setting through its history, theology, and music, and what its localisation of the Roman rite meant after the Council. Peer-reviewed, open access.

featured.title: Tres Corales de Bach
featured.blurb: His edition of three Bach chorales for GIA, part of his work for Spanish-speaking parishes. He also serves on the editorial board of GIA's Spanish hymnal.

featured.title: Concert of Silences
featured.blurb: His own choral work, premiered at Concordia University Irvine. The recording is on the Listen page.
